messages:
Sophie L.: Quick sync — we need a clear playbook for demuxing the multi-tenant KV cache when noisy tenants spike. Want to avoid tail latency regressions and eviction storms.
Arjun: Are we standardizing on per-tenant score buckets or moving to a slab-based isolation first?
Sophie L.: Thinking: lightweight isolation (soft credits) + a demuxing layer that can route hot prefixes to isolated slabs if they exceed X RPS. Soft path prevents churn for small bursts.
Ben: Soft credits sound good. Curious about how we detect hot prefixes without O(n) work on every request. Metric windows?
Mira: We already emit per-prefix request counters in the sampler. We could run a tiny hot-detector every 1s that flips a flag for candidates. Cheap, approximate.
Arjun: Edge-case: rapid oscillation — hot for 2s then cold. We need hysteresis. Suggest: enter isolated slab after 3 consecutive hot ticks, leave after 10s of cool ticks.
Ryan: +1 on hysteresis. Also we need fallback policy when isolated slab runs out of space: throttle new entries or evict lowest-score tenant within slab?
Ben: Throttling new entries buys us time but might break latency SLO for that tenant. Prefer eviction within slab by tenant-score with a grace window.
Sophie L.: Tradeoff summary: 1) Soft credits = less churn but weaker isolation. 2) Isolated slab = stronger isolation but more memory. 3) Throttle = predictable cost but harms tenant latency. We should offer configurable per-customer policy.
Arjun: Interface proposal for runtime API: 
```
// annotate request path
CacheHints { tenant_id: string, prefix: string, hints: ["read-heavy", "streaming"] }
// runtime returns: route -> {shared|isolated: slab_id}
```
This keeps router simple.
Mira: We also need metrics: per-slab residency, eviction-reasons, time-in-isolation. These drive auto-heal and rebalancing.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed to rk-runtime-canary-3 at 2026-03-18T09:05:12Z :white_check_mark:
Sophie L.: Good callout on metrics. Add churn-rate and cross-tenant-eviction-count. Ops needs alert if cross-tenant evictions > 10/min.
Ryan: Implementation detail: moving a prefix to isolated slab requires copying KV entries or moving references? Copying is expensive. Can we do pointer indirection (prefix->slab pointer) and lazy-migrate values on access?
Ben: Lazy migration wins for cost. Implementation: update shard directory to point to new slab, mark entries as relocated; first access pulls value and writes to new location. Need to handle concurrent readers/writers.
Arjun: Concurrency: use a relocation lock per-prefix (small hot map). Readers check relocation flag, if set they read from old location and invoke a background migrator if they are the first. Use CAS to avoid thundering herd.
Mira: For correctness we must maintain read-after-write semantics during migration. Solution: writes during relocation go to the new slab with a tombstone marker in the old location, readers check both. Slightly messy but doable.
Sophie L.: Action items:
- Arjun + Ben: prototype pointer-indirection + lazy-migrate spike (2w).
- Mira: add metrics plan & alert thresholds (this week).
- Ryan: write up concurrency model and failure modes (3 business days).
Sophie L.: Also decide default policy: start with soft-credits + auto-isolate on sustained hot (3 ticks) + lazy-migrate. We'll allow per-customer override. Any objections?
Ben: No objections. Sounds safe.
Arjun: Fine by me. Will sketch the runtime API changes in the spike.
Mira: I'll add dashboards for canary before we flip defaults.
Sophie L.: Thanks — posting plan to the RFC follow-up doc. Ping me if you need more context. :memo:
ops-bot: Reminder: weekly cache-health report will include new slab eviction metrics starting next Monday.
